title.zh: 卷七 本紀第七 前廢帝
title.raw: 卷七 本紀第七 前廢帝 Volume 7 Annals 7: Emperor Fei I

sentences.zh: 前廢帝諱子業，小字法師，孝武帝長子也。

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor's taboo name was Ziye; his childhood name was Fashi. He was the eldest son of Emperor Xiao Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Fei I, whose personal name was Ziye and childhood name Fashi, was Emperor Xiao Wu's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年正月甲申生。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, on the day jiashen, he was born.
translations.idiomatic: He was born on jiashen day in the first month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮尋陽，子業留京邑。

translations.literal: When Shizu garrisoned Xunyang, Ziye remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: While Shizu held Xunyang, Ziye stayed behind in the capital.

sentences.zh: 三十年，世祖入伐元凶，被囚侍中下省，將見害者數矣，卒得無恙。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when Shizu entered to attack the arch-criminal, he was imprisoned in the Attendant's Lower Bureau of the Secretariat; he was several times on the verge of being killed, but in the end came to no harm.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, when Shizu marched in to punish the arch-criminal, Ziye was held prisoner in the Attendant's Lower Bureau of the Secretariat. He was nearly killed more than once, yet ultimately escaped unharmed.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, Ziye was installed as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizu took the throne, Ziye was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 始未之東宮，中庶子、二率並入直永福省。

translations.literal: At first he had not yet gone to the Eastern Palace; the palace aides and the two commandants all entered duty at Yongfu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He had not yet moved into the Eastern Palace; his tutors and the two commandants of the guard all attended him at Yongfu Province instead.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，出居東宮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming, he moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming he took up residence in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: [1]四年，講孝經於崇正殿。

translations.literal: [1] In the fourth year, he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: [1] In the fourth year he expounded the Classic of Filial Piety in Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 七年，加元服。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he received the cap-and-gown of adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he underwent the capping ceremony.

sentences.zh: 八年閏五月庚申，世祖崩，其日，太子即皇帝位。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of the eighth year, on gengshen day, Shizu died; that same day the heir apparent assumed the imperial position.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day in the intercalary fifth month of the eighth year Shizu died, and the crown prince ascended the throne that same day.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 太宰江夏王義恭解尚書令，加中書監，驃騎大將軍柳元景加尚書令。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor, Prince of Jiangxia Yi Gong, was relieved of the post of Director of the Masters of Writing and given the additional office of Supervisor of the Secretariat; the General-in-Chief Who Quells Barbarians Liu Yuanjing was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yi Gong relinquished the directorship of the Masters of Writing and was named supervisor of the secretariat; General-in-Chief Who Quells Barbarians Liu Yuanjing became director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 甲子，置錄尚書，太宰江夏王義恭錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On jiazi day the office of Recorder of the Masters of Writing was established; the Grand Preceptor, Prince of Jiangxia Yi Gong, was Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day the post of recorder of the Masters of Writing was created, with Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yi Gong filling it.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍柳元景加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: The General-in-Chief Who Quells Barbarians Liu Yuanjing was given the additional rank of Bearer of the Staff with equal protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjing, general-in-chief who quells barbarians, was also made bearer of the staff with protocol equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹永嘉王子仁為南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: The Director of the Capital Yin, Prince of Yongjia Zi Ren, was made Inspector of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Director of the Capital Prince of Yongjia Zi Ren was appointed inspector of South Yuzhou.

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker two.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note 2.

sentences.zh: 六月辛未，詔曰：「朕以眇身，夙紹洪業，敬御天威，欽對靈命。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on xinwei day, an edict said: "I, with my slight person, from early youth have inherited the great enterprise, reverently upholding Heaven's majesty and respectfully facing the numinous mandate.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day in the sixth month an edict declared: "I, young as I am, have from childhood inherited the great enterprise, reverently bearing Heaven's majesty and answering the sacred mandate.

sentences.zh: 仰遵凝緒，日鑒前圖，實可以拱默守成，詒風長世。

translations.literal: Looking up I follow the settled tradition; day by day I take the former models as my mirror—truly one may fold one's arms in silence, guard the accomplishment, and hand down good customs for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Upholding the settled tradition and taking earlier models as my daily mirror, I might indeed fold my arms, guard what has been won, and let good customs endure for generations.

sentences.zh: 而寶位告始，萬宇改屬，惟德弗明，昧于大道。

translations.literal: Yet as the precious throne is just announced and the ten thousand realms change their allegiance, my virtue is not yet clear and I am still obscure to the Great Way.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the throne has only just been announced and the realm has changed hands; my virtue is not yet manifest and I remain blind to the Great Way.

sentences.zh: 思宣睿範，引茲簡恤，可具詢執事，詳訪民隱。

translations.literal: I wish to proclaim the enlightened norm and extend this simple compassion; let all responsible offices be consulted in detail and the people's hardships thoroughly investigated.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to proclaim enlightened policy and extend this simple mercy: let every responsible office be consulted and every hardship among the people thoroughly investigated.

sentences.zh: 凡曲令密文，繁而傷治，[3]關市僦稅，事施一時，而姦吏舞文，妄興威福，加以氣緯舛互，[4]偏頗滋甚。

translations.literal: Whatever covert ordinances and secret statutes are numerous and harm good governance, [3] market tolls and transit taxes imposed for a single occasion, while corrupt clerks manipulate the text and presumptuously wield authority, together with erratic shifts in the qi of the seasons, [4] partiality and excess grow ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever covert statutes and secret regulations are so numerous that they harm governance, [3] or market tolls and transit taxes imposed only for a moment while corrupt clerks twist the wording and abuse their power, and where the seasons' qi fall out of step [4] so that bias and excess grow worse by the day—

sentences.zh: 宜其寬傜輕憲，以救民切。

translations.literal: It is fitting to broaden corvée relief and lighten punishments to rescue the people's urgent distress.
translations.idiomatic: it is fitting to ease corvée burdens and lighten punishments to relieve the people's urgent distress.

sentences.zh: 御府諸署，事不須廣，雕文篆刻，無施於今。

translations.literal: Affairs in the various bureaus of the Imperial Household need not be broad; carved patterns and seal engraving have no place in the present.
translations.idiomatic: The various offices of the imperial household need not be so numerous; carved ornament and seal engraving have no place today.

sentences.zh: 悉宜并省，以酬氓願。

translations.literal: All should be combined and reduced to answer the common people's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: All such offices should be merged and cut back to answer the people's wishes.

sentences.zh: 藩王貿貨，壹皆禁斷。

translations.literal: Princely commercial traffic is entirely forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Trade conducted by princes is forbidden altogether.

sentences.zh: 外便具條以聞。

translations.literal: Outside, let detailed lists be prepared and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Let detailed lists be prepared and reported from the provinces.

sentences.zh: 」戊寅，以豫州之淮南郡復為南梁郡，復分宣城還置淮南郡。

translations.literal: " On wuyin day the Huainan commandery of Yuzhou was restored as the Southern Liang commandery, and a portion of Xuancheng was again set apart to establish Huainan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " On wuyin day the Huainan commandery within Yuzhou was restored as Southern Liang commandery, and part of Xuancheng was again separated to re-establish Huainan commandery.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以南海太守袁曇遠為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengchen day the Administrator of Nanhai Yuan Tan-yuan was made Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day Yuan Tan-yuan, administrator of Nanhai, was appointed inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己亥，鎮軍將軍、雍州刺史晉安王子勛改為江州刺史，中護軍宗慤為安西將軍、雍州刺史，鎮北將軍、徐州刺史湘東王彧為護軍將軍，中軍將軍義陽王昶為征北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on jihai day, the General Who Pacifies the Army, Prince of Jin'an Zi Xun, was changed to Inspector of Jiangzhou; the Champion of the Army Zong Que was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou; the General Who Pacifies the North, Prince of Xiangdong Yu, was made General Who Protects the Army; the General of the Central Army, Prince of Yiyang Chang, was made General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day in the seventh month of autumn, General Who Pacifies the Army Prince of Jin'an Zi Xun was transferred to inspector of Jiangzhou; Champion of the Army Zong Que became general who pacifies the west and inspector of Yongzhou; General Who Pacifies the North Prince of Xiangdong Yu was made general who protects the army; General of the Central Army Prince of Yiyang Chang was made general who campaigns north and inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，婆皇國遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: On gengxu day the state of Pohuang sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day the state of Pohuang sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 崇皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: The Honored Empress Dowager was styled Grand Empress Dowager, and the Empress was styled Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The honored empress dowager was elevated to grand empress dowager, and the empress to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，罷南北二馳道。

translations.literal: On yimao day the northern and southern imperial speedways were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day the northern and southern imperial speedways were abolished.

sentences.zh: 孝建以來所改制度，還依元嘉。

translations.literal: Institutions altered since the Xiaojian era were restored according to the Yuanjia regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Institutional changes made since the Xiaojian era were rolled back to Yuanjia practice.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，追崇獻妃為獻皇后。

translations.literal: On bingchen day the Offered Consort was posthumously honored as Offered Empress.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day the offered consort was posthumously honored as offered empress.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，撫軍將軍、南徐州刺史新安王子鸞解領司徒。

translations.literal: On yichou day the General Who Comforts the Army, Prince of Xin'an Zi Luan, was relieved of his concurrent post as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day General Who Comforts the Army Prince of Xin'an Zi Luan was relieved of his concurrent duties as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 八月丁卯，領軍將軍王玄謨為鎮北將軍、青冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on dingmao day, the General Who Leads the Army Wang Xuanmo was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day in the eighth month, General Who Leads the Army Wang Xuanmo was made general who pacifies the north and inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.

sentences.zh: [5]己巳，以青、冀二州刺史蕭惠開為益州刺史。

translations.literal: [5] On jisi day the Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces Xiao Hui-kai was made Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: [5] On jisi day Xiao Hui-kai, inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, was appointed inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 己丑，[6]皇太后崩。

translations.literal: On jichou day [6] the Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day [6] the empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 京師雨水。

translations.literal: In the capital region rain fell in torrents.
translations.idiomatic: Torrential rain fell in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，[7]遣御史與官長隨宜賑卹。

translations.literal: On gengyin day [7] censors were dispatched together with local officials to provide relief as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day [7] censors were sent out with local officials to provide relief wherever it was needed.

sentences.zh: 九月辛丑，護軍將軍湘東王彧為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinchou day, the General Who Protects the Army, Prince of Xiangdong Yu, was made General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day in the ninth month, General Who Protects the Army Prince of Xiangdong Yu was made general who leads the army.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以尚書左僕射劉遵考為特進、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On guimao day the Left Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Zun-kao was made Special Advanced Grandee and Right Grandee for Splendid Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day Left Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Zun-kao was made special advanced grandee and right grandee for splendid virtue.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，文穆皇后祔葬景寧陵。

translations.literal: On yimao day the Cultured and Solemn Empress was enshrined at Jingning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day the Cultured and Solemn Empress was enshrined at Jingning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲戌，太常建安王休仁為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on jiaxu day, the Director of Ceremonies, Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren, was made General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day in the tenth month of winter, Director of Ceremonies Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren was made general who protects the army.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，輔國將軍宗越為司州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuyin day the General Who Assists the State Zong Yue was made Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day General Who Assists the State Zong Yue was appointed inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: [8]庚辰，原除揚、南徐州大明七年逋租。

translations.literal: [8] On gengchen day overdue rents from the seventh year of Daming in Yang and South Xuzhou were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: [8] On gengchen day overdue rents from the seventh year of Daming in Yang and South Xuzhou were remitted.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙酉，以尚書右僕射顏師伯為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yiyou day, the Right Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shi-bo was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day in the twelfth month, Right Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shi-bo was made director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: [9]壬辰，以王畿諸郡為揚州，以揚州為東揚州。

translations.literal: [9] On renchen day the commanderies of the imperial domain were made Yang Province, and Yang Province was made East Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: [9] On renchen day the commanderies of the imperial domain were constituted as Yang Province, while Yang Province itself was redesignated East Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以車騎將軍、揚州刺史豫章王子尚為司徒、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On guisi day the General of Chariots and Cavalry, Inspector of Yangzhou, Prince of Yuzhang Zi Shang, was made Minister of Works and Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day General of Chariots and Cavalry and inspector of Yangzhou Prince of Yuzhang Zi Shang was made minister of works and inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 去歲及是歲，東諸郡大旱，甚者米一升數百，京邑亦至百餘，餓死者十有六七。

translations.literal: In the previous year and this year great drought struck the eastern commanderies; in the worst places a sheng of grain cost several hundred cash, and even in the capital it rose to more than a hundred; those who starved to death were six or seven out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: In the previous year and this year the eastern commanderies suffered severe drought; in the worst-hit districts a sheng of grain cost several hundred cash, and even in the capital more than a hundred, so that six or seven out of every ten people starved to death.

sentences.zh: 孝建以來，又立錢署鑄錢，百姓因此盜鑄，錢轉偽小，商貨不行。

translations.literal: Since the Xiaojian era mints had also been established to cast coin; because of this the common people illicitly cast as well, the money grew ever more false and small, and commerce ceased to circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xiaojian era government mints had been set up to cast coin, prompting widespread illicit casting among the people; the currency grew ever more debased and light, and trade ground to a halt.

sentences.zh: 永光元年春正月乙未朔，改元。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the first year of Yongguang, on yiwei day, the first day of the month, the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day, the new moon of the first month of spring in the first year of Yongguang, the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，省諸州臺傳。

translations.literal: On yisi day the provincial relay offices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day the provincial relay offices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以領軍將軍湘東王彧為衞將軍、南豫州刺史，護軍將軍建安王休仁為領軍將軍，祕書監山陽王休祐為豫州刺史，左衞將軍桂陽王休範為中護軍，南豫州刺史尋陽王子房為東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuwu day the General Who Leads the Army, Prince of Xiangdong Yu, was made General of the Guard and Inspector of South Yuzhou; the General Who Protects the Army, Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren, was made General Who Leads the Army; the Supervisor of the Secretariat, Prince of Shanyang Xiu You, was made Inspector of Yuzhou; the General of the Left Guard, Prince of Guiyang Xiu Fan, was made Champion of the Army; the Inspector of South Yuzhou, Prince of Xunyang Zi Fang, was made Inspector of East Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day General Who Leads the Army Prince of Xiangdong Yu was made general of the guard and inspector of South Yuzhou; General Who Protects the Army Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren became general who leads the army; Supervisor of the Secretariat Prince of Shanyang Xiu You was made inspector of Yuzhou; General of the Left Guard Prince of Guiyang Xiu Fan was made champion of the army; and Inspector of South Yuzhou Prince of Xunyang Zi Fang was made inspector of East Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二月乙丑，減州郡縣田祿之半。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yichou day, the field salaries of provinces, commanderies, and counties were reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day in the second month, the field salaries paid to provincial and county officials were cut by half.

sentences.zh: [10]庚寅，鑄二銖錢。

translations.literal: [10] On gengyin day two-zhu coin was cast.
translations.idiomatic: [10] On gengyin day two-zhu coin was cast.

sentences.zh: 三月甲辰，罷臨江郡。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiachen day, Linjiang commandery was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day in the third month Linjiang commandery was abolished.

sentences.zh: 五月己亥，割郢州隨郡屬雍州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jihai day, Suo commandery of Yingzhou was detached and placed under Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day in the fifth month Suo commandery in Yingzhou was transferred to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以後軍司馬張牧為交州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingwu day the Rear Army Major Zhang Mu was made Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day Rear Army Major Zhang Mu was appointed inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 六月己巳，左軍長史劉道隆為梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jisi day, the Left Army Chief Clerk Liu Dao-long was made Inspector of Liang and South Qin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day in the sixth month Left Army Chief Clerk Liu Dao-long was made inspector of Liang and South Qin provinces.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，安西將軍、雍州刺史宗慤卒。

translations.literal: On yihai day the General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Yongzhou Zong Que, died.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day General Who Pacifies the West and inspector of Yongzhou Zong Que died.

sentences.zh: 壬午，衞將軍、南豫州刺史湘東王彧改為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On renwu day the General of the Guard, Inspector of South Yuzhou, Prince of Xiangdong Yu, was changed to Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day General of the Guard and inspector of South Yuzhou Prince of Xiangdong Yu was transferred to inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: [11]尚書令、驃騎大將軍柳元景加南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: [11] The Director of the Masters of Writing, General-in-Chief Who Quells Barbarians Liu Yuanjing was given the additional post of Inspector of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: [11] Director of the Masters of Writing and General-in-Chief Who Quells Barbarians Liu Yuanjing was also made inspector of South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋八月辛酉，越騎校尉戴法興有罪，賜死。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, on xinyou day, the Commandant of Elite Cavalry Dai Fa-xing committed an offense and was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day in the eighth month of autumn Commandant of Elite Cavalry Dai Fa-xing was found guilty and ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以尚書僕射顏師伯為尚書左僕射，[12]吏部尚書王景文為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On gengwu day the Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shi-bo was made Left Director of the Masters of Writing; [12] the Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Jing-wen was made Right Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shi-bo was made left director of the Masters of Writing; [12] Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Jing-wen was made right director.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，帝自率宿衞兵，誅太宰江夏王義恭、尚書令驃騎大將軍柳元景、尚書左僕射顏師伯、[13]廷尉劉德願。

translations.literal: On guiyou day the emperor himself led the palace guard and executed the Grand Preceptor, Prince of Jiangxia Yi Gong, the Director of the Masters of Writing and General-in-Chief Who Quells Barbarians Liu Yuanjing, the Left Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shi-bo, [13] and the Minister of Justice Liu De-yuan.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day the emperor personally led the palace guard and had Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yi Gong, Director of the Masters of Writing and General-in-Chief Who Quells Barbarians Liu Yuanjing, Left Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shi-bo, [13] and Minister of Justice Liu De-yuan put to death.

sentences.zh: 改元為景和元年。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to the first year of Jinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The reign era was changed to Jinghe.

sentences.zh: 文武賜位二等。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials were granted two ranks of promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials were promoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 以領軍將軍建安王休仁為安西將軍、雍州刺史，衞將軍湘東王彧還為南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: The General Who Leads the Army, Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou; the General of the Guard, Prince of Xiangdong Yu, was returned to Inspector of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Leads the Army Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren was made general who pacifies the west and inspector of Yongzhou; General of the Guard Prince of Xiangdong Yu was returned to inspector of South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，司徒、揚州刺史豫章王子尚領尚書令，射聲校尉沈文秀為青州刺史，左軍司馬崔道固為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day the Minister of Works, Inspector of Yangzhou, Prince of Yuzhang Zi Shang, took charge of the Masters of Writing; the Commandant of the Archers Shen Wen-xiu was made Inspector of Qingzhou; the Left Army Major Cui Dao-gu was made Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day Minister of Works and inspector of Yangzhou Prince of Yuzhang Zi Shang assumed direction of the Masters of Writing; Commandant of the Archers Shen Wen-xiu was made inspector of Qingzhou; and Left Army Major Cui Dao-gu was made inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔曰：「昔凝神佇逸，磻溪讚道，湛慮思才，傅巖毗化。

translations.literal: On yihai day an edict said: "Of old, concentrating the spirit and waiting in ease, Panxi praised the Way; sinking thought to ponder talent, Fuyan aided transformation.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day an edict declared: "In antiquity, rulers who concentrated their spirits and waited in repose had Panxi praise the Way; those who steeped their minds to seek talent had Fuyan assist in transformation.

sentences.zh: 朕位御三極，風澄萬宇，資鈇電斷，正卯斯戮。

translations.literal: I occupy the three extremities; the winds are clear across the ten thousand realms; relying on the axe and lightning judgment, at the hour of mao the guilty were executed.
translations.idiomatic: I now stand at the summit of the cosmos and the winds are clear across the realm; wielding the axe of judgment like lightning, at the mao hour the guilty were struck down.

sentences.zh: 思所以仰宣遺烈，俯弘景祚，每結夢庖鼎，瞻言板築，有劬日昃，無忘昧旦。

translations.literal: I think how to look up and proclaim the legacy left behind, look down and extend the bright fortune; night after night I dream of the ding in the kitchen, gaze toward the plank road at Fuyan—there is toil from sun tilting to sun setting, and I do not forget the hour before dawn.
translations.idiomatic: I seek to proclaim the legacy above and extend our bright fortune below; night after night I dream of the cauldron in the kitchen and look toward the plank road at Fuyan—tireless from noon tilting to dusk, never forgetting the hour before dawn.

sentences.zh: 可甄訪郡國，招聘閭部：其有孝性忠節，幽居遯棲，信誠義行，廉正表俗，文敏博識，幹事治民，務加旌舉，隨才引擢。

translations.literal: Let the commanderies and kingdoms be examined and recruits sought in the hamlets and wards: whoever has filial nature and loyal integrity, dwells in seclusion in reclusion, keeps faith and righteous conduct, is incorrupt and exemplary in custom, is cultured, keen, and broadly learned, or is capable in affairs and governs the people—such persons are to be especially commended and promoted according to their talents.
translations.idiomatic: Let every commandery and kingdom be searched and talent sought in village and ward: whoever shows filial devotion and loyal integrity, lives in hidden retirement, keeps faith and righteous conduct, is incorrupt and a model to society, is cultured, quick, and broadly learned, or is capable in affairs and governs the people—such persons must be specially commended and promoted according to their gifts.

sentences.zh: 庶官克順，彝倫咸叙。

translations.literal: Thus officials will be able to conform, and the human relations will all be set in order.
translations.idiomatic: Then officials will perform their duties and the bonds of society will fall into order.

sentences.zh: 主者精加詳括，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: Those in charge are to examine this carefully in detail and report in accord with my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Those responsible must examine this carefully and report in accord with my intent.

sentences.zh: 」以始興公沈慶之為太尉，鎮北將軍、青冀二州刺史王玄謨為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: " The Duke of Shixing Shen Qing-zhi was made Grand Marshal; the General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces Wang Xuanmo was made General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: " Duke of Shixing Shen Qing-zhi was made grand marshal; General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Qing and Ji provinces Wang Xuanmo was made general who leads the army.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以石頭城為長樂宮，東府城為未央宮。

translations.literal: On gengchen day Stone City was made Everlasting Joy Palace and the Eastern Headquarters city was made Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day Stone City was renamed Everlasting Joy Palace and the Eastern Headquarters city Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 罷東揚州并揚州。

translations.literal: East Yangzhou was abolished and merged into Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: East Yangzhou was abolished and merged into Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以北邸為建章宮，南第為長楊宮。

translations.literal: On jiashen day the northern residence was made Jianzhang Palace and the southern mansion Changyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day the northern residence became Jianzhang Palace and the southern mansion Changyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 以冠軍將軍邵陵王子元為湘州刺史。

translations.literal: The General Who Conquers All, Prince of Shaoling Zi Yuan, was made Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers All Prince of Shaoling Zi Yuan was appointed inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，原除吳、吳興、義興、晉陵、琅邪五郡大明八年以前逋租。

translations.literal: On bingxu day overdue rents before the eighth year of Daming in Wu, Wuxing, Yixing, Jinling, and Langye—the five commanderies—were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day overdue rents before the eighth year of Daming in the five commanderies of Wu, Wuxing, Yixing, Jinling, and Langye were remitted.

sentences.zh: 己丑，復立南北二馳道。

translations.literal: On jichou day the northern and southern imperial speedways were re-established.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day the northern and southern imperial speedways were re-established.

sentences.zh: 九月癸巳，車駕幸湖熟，奏鼓吹。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guisi day, the imperial carriage visited Hushu and music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day in the ninth month the emperor visited Hushu with ceremonial music performed.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On wuxu day the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以南兗州刺史永嘉王子仁為南徐州刺史，丹陽尹始安王子真為南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengzi day the Inspector of South Yanzhou, Prince of Yongjia Zi Ren, was made Inspector of South Xuzhou; the Director of the Capital Yin, Prince of Shian Zi Zhen, was made Inspector of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Inspector of South Yanzhou Prince of Yongjia Zi Ren was made inspector of South Xuzhou, and Director of the Capital Yin Prince of Shian Zi Zhen was made inspector of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，撫軍將軍、南徐州刺史新安王子鸞免為庶人，賜死。

translations.literal: On xinchou day the General Who Comforts the Army, Inspector of South Xuzhou, Prince of Xin'an Zi Luan, was demoted to commoner status and ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day General Who Comforts the Army and inspector of South Xuzhou Prince of Xin'an Zi Luan was stripped of rank, reduced to commoner status, and ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以兗州刺史薛安都為平北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingwu day the Inspector of Yanzhou Xue An-du was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day Inspector of Yanzhou Xue An-du was made general who pacifies the north and inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁未，衞將軍湘東王彧加開府儀同三司，特進、右光祿大夫劉遵考為安西將軍、南豫州刺史，寧朔將軍殷孝祖為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On dingwei day the General of the Guard, Prince of Xiangdong Yu, was given the additional rank of Bearer of the Staff with equal protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers; the Special Advanced Grandee and Right Grandee for Splendid Virtue Liu Zun-kao was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of South Yuzhou; the General Who Pacifies the North Yin Xiao-zu was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day General of the Guard Prince of Xiangdong Yu was also made bearer of the staff with protocol equal to the Three Ducal Ministers; Special Advanced Grandee and Right Grandee for Splendid Virtue Liu Zun-kao was made general who pacifies the west and inspector of South Yuzhou; and General Who Pacifies the North Yin Xiao-zu was made inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以前梁、南秦二州刺史柳元怙復為梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: On wushen day the former Inspector of Liang and South Qin provinces Liu Yuan-gu was restored as Inspector of Liang and South Qin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day former inspector of Liang and South Qin provinces Liu Yuan-gu was reappointed to those posts.

sentences.zh: 己酉，車駕討征北將軍、徐州刺史義陽王昶，內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: On jiyou day the imperial carriage campaigned against the General Who Campaigns North, Inspector of Xuzhou, Prince of Yiyang Chang; inside and outside the capital martial law was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day the emperor marched to punish General Who Campaigns North and inspector of Xuzhou Prince of Yiyang Chang, and martial law was proclaimed throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 昶奔于索虜。

translations.literal: Chang fled to the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Chang fled to the northern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，右將軍、豫州刺史山陽王休祐進號鎮西大將軍。

translations.literal: On xinhai day the General of the Right, Inspector of Yuzhou, Prince of Shanyang Xiu You, was advanced in rank to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day General of the Right and inspector of Yuzhou Prince of Shanyang Xiu You was promoted to general who pacifies the west.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以安西長史袁顗為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiayin day the Chief Clerk of the Army Who Pacifies the West Yuan Yi was made Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day Chief Clerk of the Army Who Pacifies the West Yuan Yi was appointed inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以左民尚書劉思考為益州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuwu day the Director of the Left Bureau of the People Liu Si-kao was made Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day Director of the Left Bureau of the People Liu Si-kao was made inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 是日解嚴，車駕幸瓜步。

translations.literal: That same day martial law was lifted; the imperial carriage visited Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: That same day martial law was lifted and the emperor visited Guabu.

sentences.zh: 開百姓鑄錢。

translations.literal: The common people were permitted to cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: Private casting of coin by the common people was permitted.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸亥，曲赦徐州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on guihai day, a partial amnesty was proclaimed for Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day in the tenth month of winter a partial amnesty was proclaimed for Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On bingyin day the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren was made General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren was made general who protects the army.

sentences.zh: 己卯，東陽太守王藻下獄死。

translations.literal: On jimao day the Administrator of Dongyang Wang Zao was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day Dongyang administrator Wang Zao was thrown into prison and died there.

sentences.zh: 以宮人謝貴嬪為夫人，加虎賁靸戟，鸞輅龍旂，出警入蹕，實新蔡公主也。

translations.literal: The palace woman, Honored Consort Xie, was made Lady; she was given tiger guards with halberds trailing, an imperial carriage with dragon banners, and escort on departure and return—she was in fact the Princess of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Palace woman Honored Consort Xie was elevated to lady, granted tiger guards with trailing halberds, an imperial carriage with dragon banners, and full escort on her journeys—though she was in fact Princess of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以鎮西大將軍、豫州刺史山陽王休祐為鎮軍大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On yiyou day the General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Yuzhou, Prince of Shanyang Xiu You, was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Bearer of the Staff with equal protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day General Who Pacifies the West and inspector of Yuzhou Prince of Shanyang Xiu You was promoted to general who pacifies the army with protocol equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note 14.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬辰，寧朔將軍何邁下獄死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on renchen day, the General Who Pacifies the North Yin He Mai was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day in the eleventh month General Who Pacifies the North Yin He Mai was imprisoned and died.

sentences.zh: 新除太尉沈慶之薨。

translations.literal: The newly appointed Grand Marshal Shen Qing-zhi died.
translations.idiomatic: The newly appointed grand marshal Shen Qing-zhi died.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，立皇后路氏，四廂奏樂。

translations.literal: On renyin day the Lady of the Lu clan was installed as empress; music was performed in all four side halls.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day Lady Lu was installed as empress with music performed in all four side halls.

sentences.zh: 赦揚、南徐二州。

translations.literal: An amnesty was proclaimed for Yang and South Xu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty was proclaimed for Yang and South Xu provinces.

sentences.zh: 護軍將軍建安王休仁加特進、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The General Who Protects the Army, Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren, was given the additional ranks of Special Advanced Grandee and Left Grandee for Splendid Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Protects the Army Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren was also made special advanced grandee and left grandee for splendid virtue.

sentences.zh: 中護軍桂陽王休範遷職。

translations.literal: The Champion of the Army, Prince of Guiyang Xiu Fan, was transferred to another post.
translations.idiomatic: Champion of the Army Prince of Guiyang Xiu Fan was transferred to another post.

sentences.zh: 丁未，皇子生，少府劉勝之子也。

translations.literal: On dingwei day a prince was born—the son of the Director of the Palace Workshop Liu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day a prince was born, the son of Director of the Palace Workshop Liu Sheng.

sentences.zh: [15]大赦天下。

translations.literal: [15] A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: [15] A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 贓汙淫盜，悉皆原除。

translations.literal: Embezzlement, filth, and licentious theft were all entirely remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Crimes of embezzlement, debauchery, and theft were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 賜為父後者爵一級。

translations.literal: Those who became heirs to their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had become heirs to their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以特進、左光祿大夫、護軍將軍建安王休仁為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On renzi day the Special Advanced Grandee, Left Grandee for Splendid Virtue, and General Who Protects the Army, Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren, was made General-in-Chief Who Quells Barbarians and Bearer of the Staff with equal protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day Special Advanced Grandee, Left Grandee for Splendid Virtue, and General Who Protects the Army Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren was made general-in-chief who quells barbarians with protocol equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 戊午，南平王敬猷、廬陵王敬先、安南侯敬淵並賜死。

translations.literal: On wuwu day the Prince of Nanping Jing You, the Prince of Luling Jing Xian, and the Marquis of Annan Jing Yuan were all ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day Prince of Nanping Jing You, Prince of Luling Jing Xian, and Marquis of Annan Jing Yuan were all ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 時帝凶悖日甚，誅殺相繼，內外百司，不保首領。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor's ferocity and perversity grew daily worse; executions followed one upon another, and within and without the hundred offices none could be sure of keeping his head.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor's cruelty and perversity grew worse by the day; executions came in succession, and throughout the bureaucracy no one could be sure of keeping his head.

sentences.zh: 先是訛言云：「湘中出天子。

translations.literal: Earlier a false rumor had said: "From within Xiang a Son of Heaven will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a rumor had spread: "A Son of Heaven will arise from within Xiang.

sentences.zh: 」帝將南巡荊、湘二州以厭之。

translations.literal: " The emperor intended to tour the two provinces of Jing and Xiang to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor planned a southern tour of Jing and Xiang provinces to counter the omen.

sentences.zh: 先欲誅諸叔，然後發引。

translations.literal: He first wished to execute all his uncles and only then set out.
translations.idiomatic: He meant first to kill all his uncles, then set out on the tour.

sentences.zh: 太宗與左右阮佃夫、王道隆、李道兒密結帝左右壽寂之、姜產之等十一人，謀共廢帝。

translations.literal: Taizong together with his close associates Ruan Tian-fu, Wang Dao-long, and Li Dao'er secretly joined with the emperor's attendants Shou Ji-zhi, Jiang Chan-zhi, and eleven others in a plot to depose the emperor together.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong and his close advisers Ruan Tian-fu, Wang Dao-long, and Li Dao'er secretly allied with the emperor's attendants Shou Ji-zhi, Jiang Chan-zhi, and eleven others to plot his deposition.

sentences.zh: 戊午夜，帝於華林園竹林堂射鬼。

translations.literal: On wuwu night the emperor was at the Bamboo Grove Hall of Hualin Garden shooting at ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of wuwu day the emperor was in the Bamboo Grove Hall of Hualin Garden shooting at ghosts.

sentences.zh: 時巫覡云：「此堂有鬼。

translations.literal: At the time shamans had said: "This hall has ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Shamans had declared that the hall was haunted.

sentences.zh: 」故帝自射之。

translations.literal: " Therefore the emperor shot at them himself.
translations.idiomatic: So the emperor had gone there to shoot at them himself.

sentences.zh: 壽寂之懷刀直入，姜產之為副。

translations.literal: Shou Ji-zhi, carrying a blade, entered straight in; Jiang Chan-zhi served as his second.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Ji-zhi entered directly with a blade drawn; Jiang Chan-zhi followed as his second.

sentences.zh: 帝欲走，寂之追而殞之。

translations.literal: The emperor tried to flee; Ji-zhi pursued him and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tried to flee, but Ji-zhi ran him down and killed him.

sentences.zh: 時年十七。

translations.literal: He was seventeen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventeen years old.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后令曰：

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager issued an order:
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 司徒領護軍八座：子業雖曰嫡長，少稟凶毒，不仁不孝，著自髫齔。

translations.literal: To the Minister of Works who leads the protectors of the army and the eight chief ministers: Although Ziye was called the legitimate eldest son, from youth he received a vicious and poisonous nature; his lack of benevolence and filial piety were evident from his earliest years.
translations.idiomatic: To the minister of works who heads the protectors of the army and the eight chief ministers: Although Ziye was the legitimate eldest son, from childhood he showed a vicious, poisonous nature; his want of benevolence and filial piety was evident even in his earliest years.

sentences.zh: 孝武棄世，屬當辰曆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiao Wu abandoned the world, the turn of the celestial chronology fell to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiao Wu died, the turn of the calendar fell to him.

sentences.zh: 自梓宮在殯，喜容靦然，天罰重離，歡恣滋甚。

translations.literal: From the time the imperial coffin lay in mourning his face was calm and composed; Heaven's punishment severed the bond of parent and child, yet his wanton joy grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment the imperial coffin lay in state his face was calm and untroubled; though Heaven had severed the bond between parent and child, his wanton delight only grew.

sentences.zh: 逼以內外維持，忍虐未露，而凶慘難抑，一旦肆禍，遂縱戮上宰，殄害輔臣。

translations.literal: Pressed by constraints within and without he had not yet shown his cruelty, but once his viciousness could not be restrained he unleashed disaster in a single day, then wantonly slaughtered the chief ministers above and annihilated the assisting ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Held in check at first by constraints within and without, he had not yet revealed his full cruelty; but once his viciousness could no longer be contained he unleashed catastrophe in a single day, slaughtering the chief ministers and destroying his leading advisers.

sentences.zh: 子鸞兄弟，先帝鍾愛，含怨既往，枉加屠酷。

translations.literal: The brothers Zi Luan and the rest had been cherished by the late emperor; harboring old resentments, he wrongly subjected them to savage execution.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Luan and his brothers had been cherished by the late emperor; nursing old resentments, he wrongly subjected them to savage execution.

sentences.zh: 昶茂親作扞，橫相徵討。

translations.literal: Chang, a close kinsman who served as a bulwark, was wantonly subjected to punitive expeditions.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, a close kinsman who should have served as a bulwark, was subjected to arbitrary punitive campaigns.

sentences.zh: 新蔡公主逼離夫族，幽置深宮，詭云薨殞。

translations.literal: The Princess of Xincai was forced away from her husband's clan and secretly placed in the deep palace; it was falsely announced that she had died.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Xincai was torn from her husband's house, hidden in the inner palace, and falsely announced to have died.

sentences.zh: 襄事甫爾，喪禮頓釋，昏酣長夜，庶事傾遺。

translations.literal: The mourning rites for the empress dowager had barely ended when funeral observances were abruptly cast aside; through long drunken nights every affair was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's mourning had barely ended when funeral observances were cast aside; through long nights of drunkenness every affair of state was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 朝賢舊勳，棄若遺土。

translations.literal: Worthy ministers of long service were discarded like waste soil.
translations.idiomatic: Veteran ministers of long service were discarded like waste soil.

sentences.zh: 管絃不輟，珍羞備膳。

translations.literal: Pipes and strings never ceased; rare delicacies filled every meal.
translations.idiomatic: Music never ceased; rare delicacies filled every meal.

sentences.zh: 詈辱祖考，以為戲謔。

translations.literal: He cursed and insulted his ancestors, taking it as sport.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed and mocked his ancestors for sport.

sentences.zh: 行游莫止，淫縱無度。

translations.literal: His travels knew no stop; his lewdness and excess had no limit.
translations.idiomatic: His wanderings knew no limit; his lewdness and excess had no bound.

sentences.zh: 肆宴園陵，規圖發掘。

translations.literal: He held banquets in the imperial tombs and plotted to excavate them.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted in the imperial tombs and plotted their excavation.

sentences.zh: 誅剪無辜，籍略婦女。

translations.literal: He executed and cut down the innocent and seized women by force.
translations.idiomatic: He slaughtered the innocent and seized women by force.

sentences.zh: 建樹偽豎，莫知誰息。

translations.literal: He raised false heirs and none knew whose offspring they were.
translations.idiomatic: He installed false heirs, and no one knew whose children they were.

sentences.zh: 拜嬪立后，慶過恒典。

translations.literal: In elevating consorts and installing empresses his celebrations exceeded the constant statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In elevating consorts and installing an empress his celebrations exceeded all precedent.

sentences.zh: 宗室密戚，遇若婢僕，鞭捶陵曳，無復尊卑。

translations.literal: Clansmen and close kin he treated like maidservants; beating, flogging, and dragging them along, no distinction of honor remained.
translations.idiomatic: He treated imperial clansmen and close kin like maidservants, beating and dragging them about until no distinction of rank remained.

sentences.zh: 南平一門，特鍾其酷。

translations.literal: The house of Nanping in particular received his cruelest treatment.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Nanping in particular suffered his cruelest treatment.

sentences.zh: 反天滅理，顯暴萬端。

translations.literal: He reversed Heaven and extinguished principle; his open violence had ten thousand forms.
translations.idiomatic: He reversed Heaven and extinguished moral principle; his open violence took ten thousand forms.

sentences.zh: 苛罰酷令，終無紀極，夏桀、殷辛，未足以譬。

translations.literal: Harsh punishments and cruel ordinances knew no end or limit; Xia Jie and Yin Xin would not suffice for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh punishments and cruel edicts knew no end; even Xia Jie and King Zhou of Shang would not suffice for comparison.

sentences.zh: 闔朝業業，人不自保，百姓遑遑，手足靡厝。

translations.literal: The whole court was fearful; men could not preserve themselves; the common people were in turmoil and their hands and feet had nowhere to rest.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court trembled in fear and no man could preserve himself; the people were in turmoil, with nowhere to set hand or foot.

sentences.zh: 行穢禽獸，罪盈三千。

translations.literal: His conduct was filthy as beasts'; his crimes filled three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was filthy as a beast's; his crimes filled three thousand.

sentences.zh: 高祖之業將泯，七廟之享幾絕。

translations.literal: The enterprise of the High Ancestor was on the verge of perishing; the sacrifices of the seven temples were nearly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor's enterprise was on the verge of ruin; the sacrifices of the seven temples were nearly extinguished.

sentences.zh: 吾老疾沈篤，每規禍鴆，憂煎漏刻，氣命無幾。

translations.literal: I am old and my illness deep and heavy; daily I foresee the poisoned cup; anxious distress drips away the moments and my breath and life will not last long.
translations.idiomatic: I am aged and my illness deep; daily I foresee the poisoned cup, and anxious grief wears away the moments until my breath can last no longer.

sentences.zh: 開闢以降，所未嘗聞。

translations.literal: Since the opening of the age this has never been heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Since the opening of the age nothing like this has been heard.

sentences.zh: 遠近思奮，十室而九。

translations.literal: Near and far yearn to rise up; nine houses in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far alike yearn to rise against him; nine houses in ten.

sentences.zh: 衞將軍湘東王體自太祖，天縱英聖，文皇鍾愛，寵冠列藩。

translations.literal: The General of the Guard, Prince of Xiangdong Yu, by body descends from the Great Ancestor; Heaven endowed him with heroic sagacity; Emperor Wen cherished him and his favor surpassed the other princes.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Guard Prince of Xiangdong Yu descends in body from the Great Ancestor; Heaven endowed him with heroic sagacity; Emperor Wen cherished him and his favor surpassed every other prince.

sentences.zh: 吾早識神睿，特兼常禮。

translations.literal: I early recognized his divine perspicacity and treated him with special constant ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I early recognized his divine intelligence and treated him with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 潛運宏規，義士投袂，獨夫既殞，懸首白旗，社稷再興，宗祏永固，人鬼屬心，大命允集。

translations.literal: He secretly carried a great plan; men of righteousness threw aside their sleeves; once the tyrant had fallen his head was hung on the white flag; the altars of state were renewed and the ancestral temple secured forever; human and ghost alike turned their hearts to him and the great mandate was truly gathered.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly carried a great design; men of righteousness rose up; once the tyrant had fallen his head hung from the white flag; the altars of state were renewed and the ancestral temple secured; human beings and spirits alike turned their hearts to him and the great mandate was truly gathered.

sentences.zh: 且勳德高邈，大業攸歸，宜遵漢、晉，纂承皇極。

translations.literal: Moreover his merit and virtue are lofty and far-reaching; the great enterprise returns to him; it is fitting to follow Han and Jin and succeed to the imperial apex.
translations.idiomatic: His merit and virtue are lofty; the great enterprise returns to him; it is fitting that he follow Han and Jin in ascending the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 主者詳舊典以時奉行。

translations.literal: Those in charge are to examine the old statutes and carry them out in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Those responsible are to consult the old statutes and carry them out in timely fashion.

sentences.zh: 未亡人餘年不幸嬰此百艱，永尋情事，雖存若殞。

translations.literal: I, who have not yet died, in my remaining years have unfortunately encountered this hundredfold calamity; forever tracing these events in memory, though I survive it is as if I had perished.
translations.idiomatic: I, who have not yet died, have in my remaining years encountered this hundredfold calamity; whenever I recall these events, though I still live it is as though I had perished.

sentences.zh: 當復奈何！

translations.literal: What is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: What is to be done!

sentences.zh: 當復奈何！

translations.literal: What is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: What is to be done!

sentences.zh: 葬廢帝丹陽秣陵縣南郊壇西。

translations.literal: The deposed emperor was buried west of the southern suburban altar in Moling county, Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor was buried west of the southern suburban altar in Moling county, Danyang.

sentences.zh: 帝幼而狷急，在東宮每為世祖所責。

translations.literal: The emperor from youth was impatient and harsh; in the Eastern Palace he was often reproved by Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: From youth the emperor was impatient and harsh; in the Eastern Palace Shizu often reproved him.

sentences.zh: 世祖西巡，子業啟參承起居，書迹不謹，上詰讓之。

translations.literal: When Shizu toured the west, Ziye submitted reports on his daily conduct and rising and resting; his writing was not careful and the emperor questioned and reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu toured the west, Ziye submitted reports on his daily conduct; his writing was careless and the emperor questioned and reproached him.

sentences.zh: 子業啟事陳謝，上又答曰：「書不長進，此是一條耳。

translations.literal: Ziye submitted a memorial apologizing; the emperor again replied: "Your writing does not improve—this is one matter.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye submitted a memorial of apology; the emperor replied again: "Your writing does not improve—that is one matter.

sentences.zh: 聞汝素都懈怠，狷戾日甚，何以頑固乃爾邪！

translations.literal: I hear you have always been negligent and indolent, and your perversity grows worse day by day—how can you be so obstinately stupid!"
translations.idiomatic: I hear you have always been negligent, and your perversity grows worse by the day—how can you be so obstinately stupid!"

sentences.zh: 」初踐阼，受璽紱，悖然無哀容。

translations.literal: When he first ascended the throne and received the seal and cord, he was perverse and without a mournful expression.
translations.idiomatic: When he first ascended the throne and received the imperial seal and cord, his face showed perversity without a trace of mourning.

sentences.zh: 始猶難諸大臣及戴法興等，既殺法興，諸大臣莫不震懾。

translations.literal: At first he still found the great ministers and Dai Fa-xing and others difficult to deal with; after Fa-xing was killed, none of the great ministers failed to tremble in fear.
translations.idiomatic: At first he still found the great ministers and Dai Fa-xing difficult to manage; once Fa-xing was killed, none of the great ministers failed to tremble in fear.

sentences.zh: 於是又誅羣公。

translations.literal: Thereupon he again executed the host of dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he executed a host of senior officials.

sentences.zh: 元凱以下，皆被毆捶牽曳。

translations.literal: From Yuan Kai downward all were beaten, flogged, and dragged along.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuan Kai downward all were beaten, flogged, and dragged about.

sentences.zh: 內外危懼，殿省騷然。

translations.literal: Within and without there was peril; the palace offices were in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Danger threatened within and without; the palace offices were in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 初太后疾篤，遣呼帝。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager's illness first became grave, she sent to summon the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager's illness first grew grave, she sent to summon the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「病人間多鬼，可畏，那可往。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Sickrooms have many ghosts; they are fearful—how could I go there?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Sickrooms are full of ghosts—how frightening! How could I go there?"

sentences.zh: 」太后怒，語侍者：「將刀來，破我腹，那得生如此寧馨兒！

translations.literal: The empress dowager in anger told her attendants: "Bring a knife and cut open my belly—how could I have borne such a fine son!"
translations.idiomatic: In anger the empress dowager told her attendants, "Bring a knife and cut open my belly—how could I have borne such a precious son!"

sentences.zh: 」及太后崩後數日，帝夢太后謂之曰：「汝不孝不仁，本無人君之相。

translations.literal: Several days after the empress dowager's death the emperor dreamed that the empress dowager said to him: "You are unfilial and unkind; originally you had no aspect of a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Several days after the empress dowager died the emperor dreamed that she said to him, "You are unfilial and unkind; you never had the bearing of a ruler.

sentences.zh: 子尚愚悖如此，亦非運祚所及。

translations.literal: Zi Shang is stupid and perverse to this degree; he too is not within the fortune of the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Shang is as stupid and perverse as this; he too lies outside the mandate's fortune.

sentences.zh: 孝武險虐滅道，怨結人神，兒子雖多，並無天命。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiao Wu was dangerous and cruel and extinguished the Way; resentment joined human beings and spirits; though his sons were many, none had Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiao Wu was dangerous and cruel and extinguished the Way; resentment joined men and spirits; though his sons were many, none held Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 大運所歸，應還文帝之子。

translations.literal: The great fortune returns; it should revert to a son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The great fortune returns; it should revert to a son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 」其後湘東王紹位，果文帝子也。

translations.literal: Afterward Prince of Xiangdong Yu succeeded to the throne; he was indeed a son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Prince of Xiangdong Yu succeeded to the throne—and he was indeed a son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 故帝聚諸叔京邑，慮在外為患。

translations.literal: Therefore the emperor gathered his uncles in the capital region, fearing they would become a threat outside.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the emperor gathered his uncles in the capital, fearing they would become a threat if left in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 山陰公主淫恣過度，謂帝曰：「妾與陛下，雖男女有殊，俱託體先帝。

translations.literal: The Princess of Shanyin was licentious and excessive beyond measure; she said to the emperor: "Your Majesty and I, though male and female differ, both owe our bodies to the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Shanyin was licentious beyond all measure; she told the emperor, "Your Majesty and I, though man and woman differ, both owe our bodies to the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 陛下六宮萬數，而妾唯駙馬一人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ten thousand consorts in the six palaces, while I have only one consort in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: You have ten thousand women in the six palaces, while I have only my husband.

sentences.zh: 事不均平，一何至此！

translations.literal: The affair is so unequal—how can it have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: The disparity is outrageous—how can it have come to this!"

sentences.zh: 」帝乃為主置面首左右三十人；

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon set up thirty male favorites on the left and right for the princess;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon appointed thirty male favorites to attend the princess;

sentences.zh: 進爵會稽郡長公主，秩同郡王，食湯沐邑二千戶，[16]給鼓吹一部，加班劍二十人。

translations.literal: her rank was advanced to Princess of Kuaiji with the same precedence as a prince of a commandery, a fief for bathing of two thousand households, [16] one set of ceremonial music was granted, and twenty guards with ceremonial swords were added.
translations.idiomatic: her rank was raised to Princess of Kuaiji with precedence equal to a commandery prince, a fief of two thousand households for bathing, [16] one set of ceremonial music, and twenty guards bearing ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 帝每出，與朝臣常共陪輦。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went out, he and the court ministers commonly accompanied the carriage together.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went out, court ministers commonly shared his carriage.

sentences.zh: 主以吏部郎褚淵貌美，就帝請以自侍，帝許之。

translations.literal: The princess, because the Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel Chu Yuan was handsome in appearance, asked the emperor that he serve her; the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel Chu Yuan was handsome, the princess asked the emperor to assign him to her service, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 淵侍主十日，備見逼迫，誓死不回，遂得免。

translations.literal: Yuan attended the princess for ten days, was fully subjected to coercion, swore he would rather die than submit, and thus obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan attended her for ten days under relentless pressure, swore he would rather die than submit, and was at last released.

sentences.zh: 帝所幸閹人華願兒，官至散騎常侍，加將軍帶郡。

translations.literal: The eunuch Hua Yuan'er, whom the emperor favored, reached the office of Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and was given the additional rank of general with a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The favored eunuch Hua Yuan'er rose to regular attendant of scattered cavalry with the additional rank of general holding a commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝少好讀書，[17]頗識古事，自造世祖誄及雜篇章，往往有辭采。

translations.literal: The emperor from youth loved reading; [17] he was quite knowledgeable about antiquity; he himself composed the dirge for Shizu and miscellaneous compositions, which often had literary color.
translations.idiomatic: From youth the emperor loved reading; [17] he was well versed in antiquity and himself composed Shizu's dirge and various essays, which often showed literary polish.

sentences.zh: 以魏武帝有發丘中郎將、摸金校尉，乃置此二官。

translations.literal: Because Emperor Wu of Wei had the office of Director of Tomb Opening and Colonel Who Seizes Gold, he established these two offices.
translations.idiomatic: Because Emperor Wu of Wei had created the offices of director of tomb opening and colonel who seizes gold, he established these two posts.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁、山陽王休祐領之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren and the Prince of Shanyang Xiu You were placed in charge of them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren and Prince of Shanyang Xiu You were placed in charge of them.

sentences.zh: [18]其餘事迹，分見諸列傳。

translations.literal: [18] His remaining deeds are separately recorded in the various individual biographies.
translations.idiomatic: [18] His remaining deeds are recorded separately in the various biographies.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：廢帝之事行著于篇。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The deeds of the deposed emperor are set forth in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: The deeds of the deposed emperor are set forth in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 若夫武王數殷紂之釁，不能絓其萬一；

translations.literal: If King Wu numbered the crimes of King Zhou of Shang, he could not tie up one part in ten thousand;
translations.idiomatic: If King Wu of Zhou had numbered King Zhou of Shang's crimes, he could not have matched one part in ten thousand;

sentences.zh: 霍光書昌邑之過，未足舉其毫釐。

translations.literal: Huo Guang wrote down the faults of Marquis Hai of Changyi, yet could not cite one hair's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: when Huo Guang recorded Marquis Hai of Changyi's faults, he could not cite one ten-thousandth part.

sentences.zh: 假以中才之君，有一于此，足以霣社殘宗，汚宮瀦廟，況總斯惡以萃一人之體乎！

translations.literal: Suppose an emperor of middling talent—if he had even one of these, it would suffice to topple the altars and ruin the clan, defile the palace and flood the temple; how much more when all these evils were gathered in the body of a single man!
translations.idiomatic: Suppose a ruler of middling talent possessed even one such fault—it would suffice to topple the altars, ruin the clan, and defile palace and temple; how much more when every evil was gathered in a single man!

sentences.zh: 其得亡亦為幸矣。

translations.literal: That he was able to perish was also a piece of fortune.
translations.idiomatic: That he was able to die at all was itself a kind of fortune.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual collation notes

sentences.zh: 出居東宮 各本並脫「居」字，據元龜二五六補。

translations.literal: "Moved out to the Eastern Palace"—all editions omit the character "reside"; it is supplied according to Yuan Gui 256.
translations.idiomatic: "Moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace": all editions omit "reside," supplied from Yuan Gui 256.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹永嘉王子仁為南豫州刺史 「南豫」子仁傳作「南兗」。

translations.literal: "The Director of the Capital Yin, Prince of Yongjia Zi Ren, was made Inspector of South Yuzhou"—in Zi Ren's biography "South Yuzhou" is written as "South Yanzhou."
translations.idiomatic: "Director of the Capital Yin Prince of Yongjia Zi Ren was made inspector of South Yuzhou": Zi Ren's biography reads "South Yanzhou" instead.

sentences.zh: 繁而傷治 「傷」各本並作「作」，據元龜一九一改。

translations.literal: "Numerous and harm governance"—in all editions "harm" is written as "make"; it is changed according to Yuan Gui 191.
translations.idiomatic: "Numerous and harm governance": all editions read "make" for "harm," corrected per Yuan Gui 191.

sentences.zh: 氣緯舛互 「互」各本並作「玄」，蓋形近而譌，今改正。

translations.literal: "The qi of the seasons erratic and intermixed"—in all editions "intermixed" is written as "mysterious," probably a graphic error near similarity; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: "The seasons' qi erratic and intermixed": all editions read "mysterious" for "intermixed," likely a graphic error; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍王玄謨為鎮北將軍青冀二州刺史 各本「鎮北將軍」下並衍「南徐州刺史新安王子鸞為」十一字。

translations.literal: "The General Who Leads the Army Wang Xuanmo was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces"—below "General Who Pacifies the North" in all editions the eleven characters "Inspector of South Xuzhou, Prince of Xin'an Zi Luan was made" are redundantly added.
translations.idiomatic: "General Who Leads the Army Wang Xuanmo was made general who pacifies the north and inspector of Qing and Ji provinces": all editions redundantly add "inspector of South Xuzhou Prince of Xin'an Zi Luan was made" after "general who pacifies the north."

sentences.zh: 按新安王子鸞傳，不言曾為青、冀二州刺史，而王玄謨傳，言玄謨時徙為青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: According to the biography of Prince of Xin'an Zi Luan, it is nowhere stated that he ever served as Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, whereas in Wang Xuanmo's biography it states that at this time Xuanmo was transferred to Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Luan's biography never says he held Qing and Ji provinces, whereas Wang Xuanmo's biography says Xuanmo was transferred there at this time.

sentences.zh: 今訂正。

translations.literal: It is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The text is corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 己丑 各本並作「己未」。

translations.literal: "On jichou day"—in all editions it is written as "on jiwei day."
translations.idiomatic: "On jichou day": all editions read jiwei.

sentences.zh: 按是月丁卯朔，二十三日己丑，無己未、乙丑。

translations.literal: According to this month dingmao was the first day of the month; the twenty-third day was jichou—there was no jiwei or yichou.
translations.idiomatic: That month began on dingmao; the twenty-third day was jichou—neither jiwei nor yichou occurred.

sentences.zh: 今據建康實錄及通鑑改正。

translations.literal: It is now corrected according to the Jiankang Veritable Records and the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected here according to the Jiankang Veritable Records and Zizhi Tongjian.

sentences.zh: 庚寅 各本並作「庚子」。

translations.literal: "On gengyin day"—in all editions it is written as "on gengzi day."
translations.idiomatic: "On gengyin day": all editions read gengzi.

sentences.zh: 按是月丁卯朔，無庚子，二十三日己丑後，二十四日有庚寅。

translations.literal: According to this month dingmao was the first day of the month—there was no gengzi; after the twenty-third day jichou, the twenty-fourth day had gengyin.
translations.idiomatic: That month began on dingmao, so gengzi could not occur; the day after jichou on the twenty-third was gengyin on the twenty-fourth.

sentences.zh: 今改正。

translations.literal: It is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍宗越為司州刺史 「宗越」書中多誤作「宋越」，今據宗越傳改正。

translations.literal: "The General Who Assists the State Zong Yue was made Inspector of Sizhou"—in the book "Zong Yue" is often wrongly written as "Song Yue"; it is now corrected according to Zong Yue's biography.
translations.idiomatic: "General Who Assists the State Zong Yue was made inspector of Sizhou": the text often miswrites Zong Yue as Song Yue; corrected from his biography.

sentences.zh: 以下類此者皆逕改，不具校。

translations.literal: Similar cases below are all directly corrected without separate collation.
translations.idiomatic: Similar cases below are corrected without separate notes.

sentences.zh: 以尚書右僕射顏師伯為尚書僕射 「尚書僕射」各本作「尚書左僕射」，南史無「左」字。

translations.literal: "The Right Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shi-bo was made Director of the Masters of Writing"—in all editions "Director of the Masters of Writing" is written as "Left Director of the Masters of Writing"; the History of the Southern Dynasties lacks the character "left."
translations.idiomatic: "Right Vice-Director Yan Shi-bo was made director of the Masters of Writing": all editions add "left," which the History of the Southern Dynasties omits.

sentences.zh: 李慈銘宋書札記云：「左字衍，當據南史刪。

translations.literal: Li Ci-ming's Notes on the Book of Song says: "The character left is redundant and should be deleted according to the History of the Southern Dynasties."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ci-ming's Notes on the Book of Song says the character "left" is redundant and should be deleted per the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 」按是時但置尚書僕射，不分立左右。

translations.literal: " According to this time only the office of Director of the Masters of Writing was established, without separate left and right.
translations.idiomatic: " At this time only a single director of the Masters of Writing was appointed, not separate left and right offices.

sentences.zh: 今據南史刪「左」字。

translations.literal: Now according to the History of the Southern Dynasties the character "left" is deleted.
translations.idiomatic: The character "left" is now deleted per the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 減州郡縣田祿之半 宋本、三朝本、北監本、毛本及南史作「田祿」。

translations.literal: "The field salaries of provinces, commanderies, and counties were reduced by half"—the Song edition, the Three Dynasties edition, the Northern Directorate edition, the Mao edition, and the History of the Southern Dynasties read "field salaries."
translations.idiomatic: "Field salaries of provinces, commanderies, and counties were reduced by half": the Song, Three Dynasties, Northern Directorate, and Mao editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties read "field salaries."

sentences.zh: 殿本、局本作「田租」。

translations.literal: The Palace edition and the Bureau edition read "field rent."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace and Bureau editions read "field rent."

sentences.zh: 建康實錄作「祿秩」。

translations.literal: The Jiankang Veritable Records reads "salary ranks."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiankang Veritable Records reads "salary ranks."

sentences.zh: 按普減國內田租之半，非封建統治者所肯為，此必減州郡縣官吏田祿之半。

translations.literal: According to a general reduction of field rent throughout the realm by half—not something rulers of feudal order would consent to—this must be a reduction of the field salaries of provincial and commandery officials by half.
translations.idiomatic: A general halving of field rent nationwide is not something feudal rulers would accept; this must mean halving officials' field salaries.

sentences.zh: 故建康實錄改稱為「祿秩」。

translations.literal: Therefore the Jiankang Veritable Records changed the wording to "salary ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Jiankang Veritable Records changed the wording to "salary ranks."

sentences.zh: 衞將軍南豫州刺史湘東王彧改為雍州刺史 各本並脫「南」字。

translations.literal: "The General of the Guard, Inspector of South Yuzhou, Prince of Xiangdong Yu, was changed to Inspector of Yongzhou"—all editions omit the character "south."
translations.idiomatic: "General of the Guard and inspector of South Yuzhou Prince of Xiangdong Yu was changed to inspector of Yongzhou": all editions omit "south."

sentences.zh: 按明帝紀，永光元年為南豫州刺史，鎮姑孰。

translations.literal: According to the annals of Emperor Ming, in the first year of Yongguang he was Inspector of South Yuzhou, garrisoning Guni.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming's annals show that in the first year of Yongguang he was inspector of South Yuzhou, garrisoning Guni.

sentences.zh: 又按州郡志，此時南豫州鎮姑孰，而豫州則未嘗以姑孰為州治。

translations.literal: Also according to the Monograph on Provinces and Commanderies, at this time South Yuzhou was garrisoned at Guni, while Yuzhou had never taken Guni as its seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Monograph on Provinces and Commanderies shows South Yuzhou garrisoned at Guni at this time, while Yuzhou had never used Guni as its seat.

sentences.zh: 今據明帝紀補。

translations.literal: It is now supplied according to the annals of Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: "South" is supplied from Emperor Ming's annals.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射顏師伯 「尚書左僕射」各本並作「尚書僕射」，據南史改，說見前。

translations.literal: "The Left Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shi-bo"—in all editions "Left Director of the Masters of Writing" is written as "Director of the Masters of Writing"; it is changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties, as explained above.
translations.idiomatic: "Left Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shi-bo": all editions read simply "director of the Masters of Writing"; changed per the History of the Southern Dynasties, as explained above.

sentences.zh: 以鎮西大將軍豫州刺史山陽王休祐為鎮軍大將軍開府儀同三司 鎮西大將軍各本並作「鎮北大將軍」。

translations.literal: "The General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Yuzhou, Prince of Shanyang Xiu You, was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Bearer of the Staff with equal protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers"—in all editions "General Who Pacifies the West" is written as "General Who Pacifies the North."
translations.idiomatic: "General Who Pacifies the West and inspector of Yuzhou Prince of Shanyang Xiu You was made general who pacifies the army": all editions read "general who pacifies the north."

sentences.zh: 上九月辛亥下作鎮西大將軍，休祐傳亦作鎮西，今改正。

translations.literal: Above, in the ninth month on xinhai day, it is written General Who Pacifies the West, and Xiu You's biography also writes Pacifies the West; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Above, under the ninth month on xinhai day, he is called general who pacifies the west, and Xiu You's biography agrees; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 少府劉勝之子也 「劉勝」元龜一九七及二０七同本紀。

translations.literal: "The son of the Director of the Palace Workshop Liu Sheng"—"Liu Sheng" in Yuan Gui 197 and 207 matches this chapter in the same edition.
translations.idiomatic: "Son of Director of the Palace Workshop Liu Sheng": Yuan Gui 197 and 207 agree with this chapter.

sentences.zh: 符瑞志及始安王休仁傳、宋略、南史帝紀作劉矇，南史休仁傳作劉蒙。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Portents and Omina and the biographies of Prince of Shian Xiu Ren, the Song Summary, the annals in the History of the Southern Dynasties write Liu Meng; Xiu Ren's biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties writes Liu Meng.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Portents, Xiu Ren's biography, the Song Summary, and the Southern Dynasties annals write Liu Meng; Xiu Ren's biography in the Southern Dynasties writes Liu Meng.

sentences.zh: 食湯沐邑二千戶 「食」各本並作「侯」。

translations.literal: "A fief for bathing of two thousand households"—in all editions "bathing" is written as "marquis"; it is changed according to the Imperial Readings 152.
translations.idiomatic: "Fief for bathing of two thousand households": all editions read "marquis" for "bathing," corrected per Imperial Readings 152.

sentences.zh: 據御覽一五二改。

translations.literal: It is changed according to the Imperial Readings 152.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected per Imperial Readings 152.

sentences.zh: 帝少好讀書 「讀書」各本並作「講書」，據南史、元龜一九二、御覽一二八引改。

translations.literal: "The emperor from youth loved reading"—in all editions "reading" is written as "lecturing"; it is changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties, Yuan Gui 192, and the Imperial Readings 128 citation.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor from youth loved reading": all editions read "lecturing" for "reading," corrected per the History of the Southern Dynasties, Yuan Gui 192, and Imperial Readings 128.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁山陽王休祐領之 各本並脫「休仁山陽王」五字，據南史補。

translations.literal: "The Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren and the Prince of Shanyang Xiu You were placed in charge"—all editions omit the five characters "Xiu Ren, Prince of Shanyang"; they are supplied according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: "Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren and Prince of Shanyang Xiu You were placed in charge": all editions omit "Xiu Ren, Prince of Shanyang," supplied from the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 張燴讀史舉正云：「按建安王乃休仁，休祐則山陽王也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xue's Corrections in Reading History says: "According to the Prince of Jian'an is Xiu Ren, and Xiu You is the Prince of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xue's Corrections in Reading History says: "The Prince of Jian'an is Xiu Ren and Xiu You is Prince of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 南史作『以建安王休仁、山陽王休祐領之』為是。」

translations.literal: The History of the Southern Dynasties' reading 'the Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren and the Prince of Shanyang Xiu You were placed in charge' is correct."
translations.idiomatic: The History of the Southern Dynasties' reading 'Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren and Prince of Shanyang Xiu You were placed in charge' is correct."
